title: Limiter refusals that say when: shared Retry-After from the window's own state
tests_added: app/api/rate-limit-contract.test.ts (tree rule + 4 new rows + retryAfter pins)
deviations_from_card: Card acceptance 7/7. At the test-case level, 26 cases went red before the build and all are green after: 3 in rate-limit.test, 4 in throttle-response.test, 4 route-level, 1 ops, 14 contract. Following the critic note, case 5's behavioural drive runs the real limiter in the contract test. Route-level Retry-After assertions go only in the three routes whose tests already import the handler (billing/webhook, agents/report, devcase/inbound). channels/inbound and channels/webhooks/[token] get contract rows only. The Window type now stores `limit`, so rateLimitRetryAfterMs returns null for a window that still has room, not only for unknown or reset keys. That rule is stricter than the card's. retryAfterSeconds is an exported pure helper. withRetryAfter's windowMs is optional so tts/stt stay uncapped, matching the engine's own wait. channels/inbound, agents/report and devcase/inbound were not on the contract table, so they were added as rows at the end. The write set grew only by pins that fixed the old expression: app/_lib/auth/login-throttle.test.ts and app/api/devcase/devcase-candidate-refusals.test.ts, each updated to require the new shape and forbid the old. It also grew by the route tests of the touched routes. No perf-budget change. The contract test is a shared surface that needed the route changes to be green, so commit 2 bundles routes, contract test and doc under the lock instead of committing the shared surface alone. There was no separate test-first commit, because a test commit alone would be red. The per-commit green order is lib, then routes plus contract.
notes: tsc: the only errors are under the untracked kpi-sim/ snapshot, so exit 1 is foreign. A first run also showed transient sibling errors (apply-link-recovery.ts, reapply-capability-gate.test.ts) that cleared on re-run. test:unit exits 1 on 3 BROKEN, none of them this card's: python-runner-concurrency (the known Windows env issue from wave 2); rate-limit-contract 'tasks/[id]/retry' RETRYABLE ordering (a sibling's uncommitted edit to app/api/tasks/[id]/retry/route.ts, red on HEAD's contract too); and devcase-candidate-refusals, which was mine, has been fixed, and is green in the commit. test:perf exits 1 on about 30 lines, none on this card's routes. The new leaf throttle-response.ts is on 8 routes only. devcase/inbound measures 225/2988 KB against the 225/3000 ceiling, at the limit but passing. app/page.tsx is over at 1371 modules / 8724 KB. This card adds 0 modules and about 2.3 KB to that graph (rate-limit.ts via api-response's RATE_LIMITED_ERROR import), so HEAD's 8702 plus this card is about 8704, under 8710. The rest is sibling in-flight work (comms-dispatch, tasks, matrix). The llm-config and job-ingest lines are the known pre-existing ones. The wire is additive only: the same code, status and message go out, plus Retry-After and retryAfterSeconds on the migrated doors. No budget, key or placement changed, so no door is more permissive. /api/ops gains rateLimitRefusals (per key family, capped at 256 families, and no key material).
